Based on my network forensic analysis of the PCAP, I've identified the infected host, malware family, and all indicators of compromise.

## Incident Report

**VICTIM HOST**
- IPv4 Address: 10.1.17.215
- MAC Address: 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74
- Windows Hostname: DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ
- Logged-in User: shutchenson

**MALWARE FAMILY**
- **DynGate RAT** (Remote Access Trojan)
- **Attribution: Signature-confirmed** via multiple sources:
  - DNS query resolves to `ping3.dyngate.com`
  - HTTP beaconing to `master16.teamviewer.com/din.aspx` with explicit `client=DynGate` parameter
  - Classic DynGate C2 communication pattern on /din.aspx (upstream) and /dout.aspx (downstream) endpoints

**COMMAND AND CONTROL ENDPOINTS**

| IP Address | Port | Protocol | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.252.153.241 | 80 | HTTP | Primary C2, file hosting (earliest contact) |
| 185.188.32.26 | 80 | HTTP | DynGate C2 (master16.teamviewer.com spoofed) |
| 45.125.66.32 | 2917 | TLS | Encrypted C2 (most traffic) |
| 45.125.66.252 | 443 | HTTPS | Secondary encrypted C2 |

**MALICIOUS DOMAINS**
- ping3.dyngate.com (DynGate C2 beacon)
- master16.teamviewer.com (DynGate C2, spoofed TeamViewer)

**MALICIOUS URLS**
- http://5.252.153.241/1517096937 (beaconing endpoint)
- http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/* (file distribution)
- http://master16.teamviewer.com/din.aspx (DynGate command upstream)
- http://master16.teamviewer.com/dout.aspx (DynGate response downstream)

**TRANSFERRED FILES AND HASHES (SHA256)**

| Filename | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| pas.ps1 | 1553 bytes | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |
| 29842.ps1 | 1512 bytes | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded |
| TeamViewer | 4.38 MB | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | 653 KB | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 |
| osk | 371 KB | 1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f |

**ATTACK TIMELINE**
- t+60s: Initial C2 contact to 5.252.153.241 (HTTP C2 server)
- t+611s: DynGate beaconing to 185.188.32.26 (master16.teamviewer.com)
- t+890s: Primary encrypted C2 connection to 45.125.66.32:2917
- Throughout: Multiple PowerShell payloads and auxiliary files downloaded; persistent beaconing observed

**SUMMARY**
The compromised workstation is running DynGate RAT malware, actively beaconing to four distinct C2 infrastructure endpoints. The malware has achieved execution of obfuscated PowerShell scripts and appears to be maintaining persistent remote access. The infection demonstrates sophisticated C2 diversification (multiple protocols and IP addresses) typical of organized adversary activity.
